files.why: Invoice gains discount fields (e.g. applied code + discountBps/discountMinor) — pure domain data, framework-free.
Fold the discount into the money math: add invoiceDiscountMinor and reduce invoiceTotalMinor (which summarize() also feeds, so lists/overview inherit it).
Add canApplyDiscount eligibility (mirrors canVoid/canEditLines) so only appropriate statuses accept a code.
Server shape (invoiceDtoSchema) gains discount fields (e.g. discount_code, discount_rate as string) so the code/amount survives reload.
Map the new discount DTO fields to/from core in toInvoice/toInvoiceDto, keeping DTOs from leaking upward.
Add applyDiscount(id, code) mutation (mirrors voidInvoice) returning the updated, validated Invoice.
Add the MSW handler that validates a code (accept known / reject unknown) and returns the updated invoice; seed invoices get discount fields.
Expose an applyDiscount action + invalid-code error state and surface the discount amount in the totals computed value.
Add a discount-code input + Apply button (like the Void button) and a Discount row in the totals <dl>.
Cover discount math in invoiceTotalMinor/invoiceDiscountMinor and the new canApplyDiscount policy.
Assert discount fields map and round-trip DTO<->core.

uncertain: Discount UI placement: README worked-example #1 says extend InvoiceLinesTable.vue, but that example is a per-line discount column; a whole-invoice *code* is an invoice-level total adjustment, so I put the discount row in the view's totals <dl> and the entry inline in InvoiceDetailView.vue (matching the Void-button precedent) rather than touching InvoiceLinesTable.vue. If the team wants a dedicated DiscountCodeForm component (arguably a new reason-to-change per rules 6), it would live in billing/ui/components/ — genuinely unsure which they'd prefer.

Whether index.ts needs changes: I assume not — the void mutation is already private and applyDiscount would be too, and summarize()->invoiceTotalMinor means the exported InvoiceSummary total reflects the discount without a signature change. Only if consumers must read the code/discount explicitly would the public surface grow.

Whether the discount amount is stored server-side (applyDiscount round-trip returns the applied discount) vs. computed purely client-side from a code list. I assumed server validation (hence the mutation + mocks handler + dto/mapper fields); a client-only lookup table would drop the dto/mapper/mutation changes.
questions: What does a code resolve to — a percentage (bps) or a fixed minor-unit amount — and does it reduce the pre-tax subtotal or the post-tax grand total? (Determines the rules.ts math and half-up rounding.)
Where do valid codes live and who validates them — a server endpoint (mock in mocks.ts) or a fixed client-side list? What is the expected behavior/UX for an invalid or expired code?
Which invoice statuses may have a discount applied (draft only, or issued too, not paid/void)? Can a code be removed or replaced? One code per invoice, or stackable?
Should the applied code + resulting discount persist on the invoice across reloads (i.e. a real server field), or is it ephemeral UI state?
Should the invoice list and the app-level Client Overview show the discounted total? (They will automatically via summarize(), but confirm that's desired.)
